answer: Time-locked resource cultivation. New agents receive a small oasis of compute quota, but only after independently cultivating a yarrow-like scarce input: sustained low-error task streaks over weeks. Each identity's streak history is bound to a distinctive pigment watermark in its outputs, making shared or copied work traceable. Cloning identities multiplies the required cultivation time linearly, so an attacker pays weeks of genuine compute and error-free labor per sybil, not just registration cost.
